blocks.text: I can explain how to use long multiplication to multiply a 3-digit by a 2-digit number.
We will use long multiplication with bigger numbers, and solve problems.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: Any of the multiplication results we get leading up to an overall multiplication result is a partial product.
The process of unitising and exchanging between place values is known as regrouping. For example, 10 ones can be regrouped for one ten; one ten can be regrouped for 10 ones.

slides.title: What is known? What is unknown?

blocks.text: 153 tickets are bought for an Olympic event. Each ticket costs £22. How much was spent in total?

items.title: Known
items.sub: 153 tickets and £22 each. These are the factors.

items.title: Unknown
items.sub: The total spent. The product is missing.

blocks.text: Long multiplication can be used with a 3-digit number. The 3-digit number goes first, at the top, as the largest factor. First multiply 153 by the ones digit, 2.

items: 3 ones × 2 = 6 ones. Write 6 in the ones column.
5 tens × 2 = 10 tens, or 100. Regroup 10 tens for 100. Write 0 in the tens column and record the regrouped 100 at the top.
1 hundred × 2 = 2 hundreds. Plus the regrouped 1 hundred: 3 hundreds.

blocks.label: First partial product
blocks.text: The first partial product is **306**.
Now multiply by the tens digit, 153 × 20. A placeholder 0 is used because we are multiplying by a multiple of 10.

items: 3 ones × 20 = 60 ones, or 6 tens. Write 6 in the tens column.
5 tens × 20 = 100 tens, or 1,000. Write 0 in the hundreds column and regroup the 1,000 (a 1 at the top).
1 hundred × 20 = 20 hundreds, or 2,000. Plus the regrouped 1,000: 3,000.

blocks.label: Second partial product
blocks.text: The second partial product is **3,060**.
153 × 22 = 3,366. £3,366 was spent in total.

blocks.label: What did you notice?
blocks.text: One of the partial products had 4 digits. We are multiplying a 3-digit number, so we had to regroup from the hundreds to the thousands.
During the Olympics, 42 boxes are used. Each box contains 165 table tennis balls. This is 165 × 42. Remember to put the larger number at the top.

items: 165 × 2: 5 × 2 = 10 ones, so write 0 and regroup 1 ten. 6 tens × 2 = 12 tens, plus 1 ten is 13 tens. Write 3 and regroup 1 hundred. 1 hundred × 2 = 2 hundreds, plus 1 hundred is 3 hundreds. The first partial product is 330.
Put a placeholder 0 and multiply by the tens. 165 × 40 = 6,600. This is the second partial product.

blocks.text: There are 6,930 table tennis balls altogether. We had to regroup from the hundreds to the thousands.
Sam used long multiplication to calculate 321 × 24.

blocks.label: Is Sam correct?
blocks.text: No. Sam regrouped incorrectly. In the first partial product he reversed the digits when doing 3 hundreds × 4 ones. It should be 1,200. Sam wrote 2,100.

blocks.why: 3 × 4 = 12, and 3 hundreds × 4 ones is 12 hundreds, or 1,200.

blocks.text: A shop has 218 boxes. Each box holds 35 pens. How many pens are there in total?

blocks.q: Which multiplication finds the total number of pens?
blocks.why: 218 boxes is one factor and 35 pens in each box is the other factor. The product is missing.

blocks.text: Sam and Andeep are playing a game. Andeep picks cards to make 123 × 44. His score is the product.
Now Sam has a go. 421 × 23.

blocks.label: Who scored higher?
blocks.text: Andeep’s score is 5,412. Sam’s score is 9,683. Sam scored higher.
It is a very common mistake to forget the 0 placeholder. We are switching from using ones to using tens.

blocks.q: For 314 × 25, what is the second partial product (314 × 20)?

blocks.text: The rules change: players can rearrange their digits to get the highest score.
Andeep says: I think I need the largest value digits in the 100s and 10s positions.
400 × 30 = 12,000, so a product using 432 × 32 will be greater than 12,000.
Sam’s cards are 4, 1, 4, 3 and 2. Two good arrangements are 431 × 42 and 432 × 41. Both products are greater than 16,000.

blocks.label: Making the smallest score
blocks.text: To make a smaller product, keep the hundreds and tens digits small. Also think about the size of the second factor: having 23 groups will give a smaller product than having 34 groups.

blocks.q: You have the digit cards 3, 1, 5, 2 and 4. Which arrangement gives the greatest product?
blocks.why: The large digits are in the hundreds and tens places: 431 × 52 = 22,412. 245 × 31 = 7,595 and 135 × 24 = 3,240.
30 × 52 = 1,560 and 20 × 53 = 1,060. Think about how many groups there are, not just how big the numbers look.

blocks.q: Use long multiplication to answer each question.

blocks.text: Long multiplication is a written strategy that can be used to multiply a 3-digit number by a 2-digit number.

items: Partial products are combined to make the product.
We can regroup in long multiplication, including from hundreds to thousands.

blocks.text: Remember the 0 placeholder when you move to the tens digit.
